When does a learned rewrite help?

Inspect two recorded public development benchmarks. Each used its own inputs, candidate and cost model. Opening a case displays retained evidence. All figures come from the recorded runs.

Composite-factor qualification 423 → 32 explored states

Across 12 paired search tasks, 12/12 showed a material gain and the recording found 0 correctness regressions. The rewrite passed 12/12 positive holdouts. All 12/12 negative controls passed by emitting zero candidates.

Retained rewrite (A + 2)*x + A*x → (2*A + 2)*x

One qualification run of the shared rewrite is linked to 7 of 9 formed lineages. The tests cover one public held-out composite-factor cluster. Handoffs retain a symbolic polynomial-normal-form check. Formal proof status is NOT_EVALUATED. Explored states measure search work on these tasks.

Original qualification evidence (JSON.gz) · Registered fixture source

Cross-family transfer 53 matcher calls · 0 applications

The coefficient-gap-two bridge emitted no moves. Native factorization reached 4/4 positive targets in the baseline and 4/4 with the bridge enabled. Both arms ran every negative control, and 0 of 8 control runs reached their requested target. The recorded comparison found no held-out work reduction.

The matcher-call count includes both target types in all four families. Two families supplied untargeted formation cases and two families were held out. The paired searches used registered targets, including deliberately inequivalent negative targets. Transfer status is REJECTED_FORMATION_FAMILY, with failed positive bridge validation in every family. Proof status is NOT_EVALUATED.
